Subject: Caching economics worksheet & pilot scope

Hi Alice — thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned before I send the worksheet: 

TL;DR: You’re evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization flows. High-level asks we heard:
- Steady-state traffic: ~50M tokens/month (with bursts up to ~80M in promotional events)
- Pilot: 5M tokens over a 6-week proof-of-concept (endpoints + basic observability)
- Target unit economics: approx $1,500 / 1M tokens for steady-state to fit internal budget

Open questions we promised to quantify in the worksheet:
- Effective $/1M tokens under different prefix-cache hit-rate assumptions (10/30/60/70%)
- How prefix caching is applied (per-session prefixes, shared repository, TTL) and operational tradeoffs
- Expected latency improvement & any impact on model selection for the pilot

I’ve attached a short worksheet (savings_worksheet.xlsx) and a one-page prefix plan. The worksheet contains a simple formula-driven table you can change: base price / 1M tokens, assumed cache hit rate, and pilot vs steady-state volumes. 

Next steps: I’ll follow up in this thread with the filled worksheet and a short cost sensitivity note. If the numbers look good, can we plan to get procurement looped in the week of 6/21 for a pilot SOW?

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Evelyn — thanks for the recap and for sending materials. A couple clarifications from our end before you finalize the worksheet: 

1) Volumes: 50M tokens/month is our conservative estimate for Q4 steady-state. Peak events could push to ~80M but that’s seasonal. Pilot should be limited to 5M total tokens (6 weeks) as you noted.
2) Budget: Our finance sponsor gave a target unit economics of ~$1,500 / 1M tokens for steady-state. That’s the bar for procurement to push this forward to legal.
3) Hit-rate assumptions: We run longish prompts (patient history + context) with many repeat prefixes across sessions. We think a 40—60% prefix cache hit is plausible, but we need Redwood to show the math: what hit-rate do you need to achieve the $1,500 target?

Can you include a table that shows required hit-rate thresholds plus the expected monthly cost at 50M tokens? Procurement would like to see that as part of the pilot economics doc.

Appreciate it — Alice
Product, Brightway Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@brightwayhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Caching economics worksheet & pilot scope

Alice — great, thanks for the clear asks. Attached is the filled worksheet (savings_worksheet.xlsx). Key extracts below so procurement has a one-glance table. I’ve kept the math conservative (assume cached tokens cost 0.05x base compute) and included a small warm-layer operational surcharge ($200 / 1M on cached portion) to cover shared memory & keepalive overhead for high-concurrency deployments. Feel free to change those cells in the sheet.

Assumptions (worksheet):
- Base hosted inference list price (model variant for pilot): $2,400 / 1M tokens
- Cached-token marginal cost: 5% of base (~$120 / 1M cached tokens) + warm-layer surcharge $200 / 1M cached portion -> effective cached cost = $320 / 1M tokens (conservative)
- Pilot & steady state volumes: pilot 5M tokens, steady 50M tokens/month

Simple formula used: effective $/1M = (1 - hit_rate) * base_price + hit_rate * cached_effective_cost

Scenario table (for 50M tokens/month):
- 0% hit: effective = $2,400 -> monthly = $120,000
- 20% hit: effective = 0.8*2400 + 0.2*320 = 1,920 + 64 = $1,984 -> monthly = $99,200
- 40% hit: effective = 0.6*2400 + 0.4*320 = 1,440 + 128 = $1,568 -> monthly = $78,400
- 60% hit: effective = 0.4*2400 + 0.6*320 = 960 + 192 = $1,152 -> monthly = $57,600
- 70% hit: effective = 0.3*2400 + 0.7*320 = 720 + 224 = $944 -> monthly = $47,200

Required hit-rate to meet your $1,500 / 1M target:
Solve for hit_rate: (1 - h)*2400 + h*320 <= 1500 -> 2400 - 2400h + 320h <= 1500 -> 2400 - 2080h <= 1500 -> 2080h >= 900 -> h >= 0.433.
So roughly a 44% prefix cache hit (rounded up to 45%) gets you at or below $1,500 / 1M under the conservative cached-cost assumptions above.

Operational notes on the prefix strategy we propose in prefix_cache_plan.pdf:
- Prefix definition: first 256 tokens of the prompt + hashed user/session attributes, stored in a shared LRU store (TTL default 24h, adjustable).
- Warm-layer behavior: when a prefix is in cache we avoid full forward-pass up to that length and serve the remainder using KV-cache warmup (retains KV state for active keys). This is the basis for the cached_cost assumption.
- Tradeoffs: higher TTLs & larger cache capacity increase hit-rate but raise memory and eviction management complexity. We recommend the pilot use a 24–72h TTL and a 50k key cache size (worksheet includes sensitivity table).

I’ve included a worked example in the sheet you can paste into procurement’s packet. If you want, we can run a short synthetic replay over a week of anonymized logs to produce an expected hit-rate estimate before the pilot (we do this for prospective customers).

Attachments: savings_worksheet.xlsx (worked numbers) and prefix_cache_plan.pdf (technical approach).

Next: if the numbers look right to you, Karthik will send a pilot SOW + procurement checklist. Can procurement aim to get initial PO or approval by end of next week (6/25)?

—
Evelyn

Evelyn / team — this is exactly what procurement wanted to see. The breakdown and the conservative cached-cost assumption are helpful. Two quick asks before we loop legal: 
1) Could you run the synthetic replay on a 7-day sample we’ll send (anonymized) to validate the 44–45% hit-rate estimate? That will make procurement comfortable.
2) Please add a short note in the worksheet that pilot traffic will be excluded from any committed-volume discount calculations (we don’t want pilot math inflating steady-state forecasts).

We’ll share the sample logs by EOD today. If the replay looks similar to your estimate, procurement will push to get the pilot PO approved the week of 6/21.

Thanks — Alice
